newsitem.title: USA: TALKING POINT-Intel tackles product shift.
newsitem.headline: TALKING POINT-Intel tackles product shift.

text.p: Intel Corp is powering its way through a product transition chief executive Andrew Grove calls "monumental", but some analysts say the company and its investors face another quarter of turbulence.
Intel said Tuesday it expects revenues to be flat to just slightly higher in the third quarter compared with the $6.0 billion it reported in the June quarter just completed.
However, analysts said third quarter earnings per share estimates would be trimmed to a penny or two below the second quarter's $0.92 a share from their previous $0.98 consensus.

Intel is struggling to shift production to the new Pentium with MMX technology and Pentium II microprocessors it says customers are now demanding, and analysts said the move is resulting in even less visibility than normal in the quarter, when sales are traditionally weighted towards September.
Furthermore, Intel is expected to announce substantial price cuts in certain chips at the end of this month.

"It's hard to be aggressive here in this kind of back-end weighted quarter in front of these major price moves, in front of product transition issues," said Robert Chaplinsky, an analyst at investment bank Hambrecht & Quist. "There are just too many what-ifs."

Intel executives told analysts in a conference call the company was ahead of expectations on moving production to denser, more cost-effective 0.25 micron designs. But in several other areas, the officials said it was a difficult quarter to predict and they declined to offer specific guidance.

Robertson Stephens & Co analyst Dan Niles said he expects third quarter revenues could grow by as much as 5-10 percent. While consensus estimates may be cut now, as was expected, he said they may creep higher as the quarter progresses.
"The stock's going higher," he said. Indeed, Intel jumped more than 2 points in after-hours trade to 83.
The earnings were released after market hours. Earlier, Intel shares had closed up 2-5/32 at 80-29/32.
"In the middle of one of the worst (product) transitions in the traditionally worst quarter of the year, they're giving good guidance," added Niles.

But some analysts also commented that Intel's projection that gross margins would be flat to slightly down from the 61 percent it attained in the second quarter was benefiting from at least one non-operational windfall -- the company reduced its 1997 depreciation estimates by $300 million.

Cowen & Co. analyst Drew Peck calculated third-quarter gross margin projections would be 58 percent if the company had not had the accounting discrepancy, which Intel officials said had simply resulted from a miscalculation.
But Peck also said the stock has been driven recently more by cash inflows into the market than by fundamentals, so the impact of the change may go largely unnoticed.

"Nobody's really going to want to hear this in a bull market like this," he said. Analysts said they expect fourth-quarter consensus estimates to settle in the $0.97 to $0.98 range, somewhat below earlier consensus of $1.11.
Intel said it aims to ensure it can meet customer demand as it shifts to the new-generation processors, which it said was the company's fastest such production transition.

Grove has said Pentium with MMX multimedia technology and Pentium II processors together should account for about 90 percent of Intel's microprocessor revenues by the fourth quarter, and analysts said the shift was now imperative.
"To me, this is the last quarter to get rid of the (older) stuff," said Hambrecht & Quist's Chaplinsky. "If you can't get rid of it here, you're in trouble, because the market has switched."
